newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour wins by-election; Major's woes deepen.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour wins by-election; Major's woes deepen.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party on Thursday scored a victory in a parliamentary by-election that further weakened Prime Minister John Major's grip on power, the Press Association news agency said.
Labour's triumph in Thursday's election in the Barnsley East constituency in northern England -- a Labour stronghold -- ensured that the Conservatives no longer command a majority in parliament.

Local council leader Jeff Ennis won 14,683 votes against 1,299 for Conservative Jane Ellison, who finished third to Liberal Democrat candidate David Willis with 1,502. Ennis was defending a Labour majority of 24,777 votes won by his predecessor Terry Patchett, whose recent death led to the by-election.

The by-election was one of the last readings of public opinion before the next general election -- which must be called by May -- but the run-down, working-class constituency has long voted left of centre and is not typical of the nation at large.
The result nevertheless deepened Major's problems, coming days after he effectively lost his majority in parliament when a disgruntled Conservative MP, Sir John Gorst, withdrew support.
Even if Gorst is still formally counted as a Conservative, the party's 323 voting members of parliament are now evenly matched by legislators sitting for opposition parties.
